# Purpose

Fixes #48421-adjacent bug: on CPU, bgmv_shrink/bgmv_expand/bgmv_expand_slice (vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py) gather lora_b_weights[lora_indices_tensor] directly, including for rows whose index is -1 ("no LoRA active for this token"). There's no dedicated null slot, so -1 triggers ordinary negative indexing and silently aliases the last real adapter slot (lora_b_weights[max_loras - 1]). With the common max_loras=1 case, that's the one loaded adapter's own slot — so any batch mixing base-model-only requests with adapter-targeted requests can have the adapter's LoRA delta silently added into base-model rows' output.

Note on #48421: I found vllm-project/vllm#48421 open against the same underlying bug while doing the required duplicate-work check. That PR is correct but fixes it by clamping the index to 0 and zeroing the result afterward (masked_fill) — the full shrink/expand GEMM still runs on every no-op row. This PR instead masks out invalid rows before the gather + einsum, so no-op rows cost nothing (and a batch with zero active LoRA rows returns immediately without any GEMM at all). It also fuses add_shrink's per-slice Python loop across lora_a slices into a single batched op in PunicaWrapperCPU, removing the existing # TODO fuse these kernels — a related but separate gap in the same code path, not covered by #48421. Happy to defer to #48421 for the minimal fix if maintainers prefer the smaller diff; opening this as an alternative given the additional performance benefit and the unaddressed fusion TODO.

# Test Plan

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -v -k "no_lora or shrink_skips or expand_skips or expand_slice_skips"
pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py

Added three regression tests covering mixed batches (max_loras=1, some rows -1) for bgmv_shrink, bgmv_expand, and bgmv_expand_slice, each asserting no-op rows are left untouched (not aliased with the loaded adapter's delta) and active rows still get the correct value.

# Test Result

tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py::test_bgmv_shrink_skips_no_lora_rows PASSED
tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py::test_bgmv_expand_skips_no_lora_rows PASSED
tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py::test_bgmv_expand_slice_skips_no_lora_rows PASSED
3 passed

All three new tests fail against the pre-fix implementation (confirmed: no-op rows pick up nonzero values equal to the aliased adapter delta) and pass against this fix.

pre-commit run (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy, typos, SPDX headers) passes on all changed files.

No model-level eval was run — this is a kernel-correctness fix with no effect on numerical results for valid (non--1) rows; the regression tests are the appropriate cheapest-level check per AGENTS.md's test-design guidance.

---
AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change. I have reviewed every changed line and run the tests and pre-commit checks above.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

**Update: this PR is now a CPU LoRA performance change.** It skips compute for no-LoRA rows in the torch bgmv ops and groups multi-slice `add_shrink` into one GEMM per active adapter: up to ~4.7x faster `add_lora_linear` in the decode path with LoRA tokens, and near-zero cost for batches with no LoRA tokens.

#48421 has since merged the minimal fix for the `-1` aliasing bug this PR originally targeted, so, as suggested on #48421, I've rebased onto it and kept the title for continuity. The correctness fix and its regression test now come from #48421; this PR changes only how the work is done. The description above predates this; the current scope is:

**1. Skip no-LoRA rows instead of computing and masking them** (`vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py`)

#48421 clamps the index to 0, runs the gather + einsum for every row, then zeroes the `-1` rows. The gather materializes a per-token copy of the LoRA weights, so base-model tokens pay the full LoRA cost. The CPU decode path also has no `no_lora` early return (prefill does), so a decode batch with no LoRA tokens still runs shrink/expand in every LoRA layer.

This PR selects only valid rows before the gather + einsum in `bgmv_shrink` / `bgmv_expand` / `bgmv_expand_slice`, and returns immediately when no row has an active adapter. Semantics match #48421 and the Triton kernels: no-LoRA rows are left untouched (including under `add_inputs=False`). When every row is valid, the original code path runs unchanged.

**2. Group `add_shrink` by LoRA** (`vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py`)

Replaces the per-slice loop (`# TODO fuse these kernels`) for multi-slice layers (e.g. packed qkv) with one GEMM per active LoRA against its concatenated A slices, with tokens sorted by LoRA. This avoids per-token weight copies entirely for shrink, which dominate cost as the batch grows. Single-slice layers keep the existing path.

**3. Benchmark** — `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py` times `PunicaWrapperCPU.add_lora_linear` (shrink + expand) in the decode path across batch sizes and LoRA/base-model token mixes.

`torch.compile` note: the CPU platform sets `CompilationMode.NONE` whenever LoRA is enabled (`vllm/platforms/cpu.py`), so the data-dependent shapes here don't introduce graph breaks.

### Not a duplicate

#48421 (merged) fixed the correctness bug with clamp + mask; this PR keeps its semantics and its regression test (`test_torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens`) and changes only how the work is done. My original aliasing tests were dropped as redundant with that test. No other open PR touches `PunicaWrapperCPU` or the torch bgmv ops. #47951 (open) skips the whole LoRA layer path in eager mode when a batch has no active adapter, but only wires that up for the GPU/XPU wrappers; it would be complementary here (layer-level skip for all-base-model batches) and doesn't cover mixed batches or the shrink grouping.

### Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens
pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py \
    vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py
python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py --max-loras 1 --iters 200
python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py --max-loras 4 --iters 200
```

Plus an out-of-tree equivalence check against #48421's implementation:
- bgmv ops: all-valid / mixed / all-`-1` batches, fp32 + bf16, `add_inputs` True/False — outputs identical (`torch.equal`).
- grouped `add_shrink` vs. the per-slice loop: decode and prefill metadata, 2–3 slices, bf16 inputs into fp32 buffers, buffers pre-filled with random values to confirm `-1` rows are untouched — `assert_close` passes; empty batch handled.

`tests/lora/test_layers.py` exercises `add_shrink` end to end on CPU (`test_column_parallel_packed`, `test_merged_column_parallel_variable_slice`), but it couldn't run in my local environment (fails identically on unmodified main); relying on CI for those.

### Test Result

- Regression test: 1 passed. Pre-commit: passed. Equivalence checks: passed.

**Benchmark** — median latency of one `add_lora_linear` call, GQA qkv-shaped packed layer (hidden 4096, output slices 4096/1024/1024), rank 16, bf16, 200 iterations, decode path; LoRA tokens are randomly interleaved with base-model tokens and spread round-robin across adapters.

**`--max-loras 1` (vLLM default)**

The one regression: with multiple adapters and very few tokens per adapter (8 tokens across 4 adapters, i.e. ≤2 tokens each), the grouped shrink is 0.89–0.97x of main (~0.1 ms per packed layer), from per-adapter op overhead. From ~16 tokens per active adapter up it wins, and it wins everywhere in the single-adapter default.

No model eval: outputs are unchanged for valid rows (bgmv path identical; grouped shrink equivalent within fp tolerance), and no-LoRA semantics match #48421.

@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import itertools
+import time
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.lora.layers import LoRAMapping
+from vllm.lora.punica_wrapper.punica_cpu import PunicaWrapperCPU
+from vllm.utils.argparse_utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE, set_random_seed
+
+# Enable AMX tile data registers so isolated runs don't rely on other operations
+# to trigger oneDNN's _init_amx() first (which can cause hangs otherwise).
+if torch.cpu._is_amx_tile_supported():
+    torch.cpu._init_amx()
+
+
+def make_index_mapping(
+    num_tokens: int, lora_fraction: float, max_loras: int, seed: int
+) -> list[int]:
+    """Per-token LoRA ids: 0 is base model, 1..max_loras are adapters."""
+    num_lora_tokens = round(num_tokens * lora_fraction)
+    ids = [i % max_loras + 1 for i in range(num_lora_tokens)]
+    ids += [0] * (num_tokens - num_lora_tokens)
+    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(seed)
+    return [ids[i] for i in torch.randperm(num_tokens, generator=g).tolist()]
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def bench_add_lora_linear(
+    num_tokens: int,
+    lora_fraction: float,
+    hidden_size: int,
+    output_slices: tuple[int, ...],
+    rank: int,
+    max_loras: int,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    iters: int,
+    seed: int = 0,
+) -> list[float]:
+    set_random_seed(seed)
+    punica = PunicaWrapperCPU(max(num_tokens, 1), 256, "cpu")
+    index_mapping = make_index_mapping(num_tokens, lora_fraction, max_loras, seed)
+    punica.update_metadata(
+        LoRAMapping(index_mapping, index_mapping, is_prefill=False),
+        list(range(1, max_loras + 1)),
+        max_loras,
+        vocab_size=32000,
+    )
+
+    lora_a = tuple(
+        torch.randn(max_loras, 1, rank, hidden_size, dtype=dtype) for _ in output_slices
+    )
+    lora_b = tuple(
+        torch.randn(max_loras, 1, size, rank, dtype=dtype) for size in output_slices
+    )
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=dtype)
+    y = torch.zeros(num_tokens, sum(output_slices), dtype=dtype)
+
+    def run(n: int) -> list[float]:
+        times = []
+        for _ in range(n):
+            start = time.perf_counter_ns()
+            punica.add_lora_linear(y, x, lora_a, lora_b, 1.0, output_slices)
+            times.append((time.perf_counter_ns() - start) / 1e6)
+        return times
+
+    run(5)
+    return run(iters)
+
+
+def main(
+    num_tokens: list[int],
+    lora_fractions: list[float],
+    hidden_size: int,
+    output_slices: tuple[int, ...],
+    rank: int,
+    max_loras: int,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    iters: int,
+    seed: int = 0,
+) -> list[dict]:
+    results = []
+    print(f"{'num_tokens':>10} {'lora_frac':>9} {'median_ms':>10} {'mean_ms':>9}")
+    for t, frac in itertools.product(num_tokens, lora_fractions):
+        times = bench_add_lora_linear(
+            t, frac, hidden_size, output_slices, rank, max_loras, dtype, iters, seed
+        )
+        median, mean = float(np.median(times)), float(np.mean(times))
+        results.append(
+            dict(num_tokens=t, lora_fraction=frac, median_ms=median, mean_ms=mean)
+        )
+        print(f"{t:>10} {frac:>9.2f} {median:>10.3f} {mean:>9.3f}")
+    return results
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = FlexibleArgumentParser(
+        description="Benchmark PunicaWrapperCPU.add_lora_linear in the decode "
+        "path with a mix of LoRA and base-model tokens."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--num-tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 8, 32, 128, 256]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--lora-fractions", type=float, nargs="+", default=[0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0]
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--hidden-size", type=int, default=4096)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--output-slices",
+        type=int,
+        nargs="+",
+        default=[4096, 1024, 1024],
+        help="Packed output slice sizes; the default is a GQA qkv_proj.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--rank", type=int, default=16)
+    parser.add_argument("--max-loras", type=int, default=4)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--dtype", type=str, choices=["half", "bfloat16", "float"], default="bfloat16"
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=50)
+    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    print(args)
+
+    main(
+        num_tokens=args.num_tokens,
+        lora_fractions=args.lora_fractions,
+        hidden_size=args.hidden_size,
+        output_slices=tuple(args.output_slices),
+        rank=args.rank,
+        max_loras=args.max_loras,
+        dtype=STR_DTYPE_TO_TORCH_DTYPE[args.dtype],
+        iters=args.iters,
+        seed=args.seed,
+    )

**Update: this PR is now a CPU LoRA performance change.** It skips compute for no-LoRA rows in the torch bgmv ops and groups multi-slice `add_shrink` into one GEMM per active adapter: up to ~4.7x faster `add_lora_linear` in the decode path with LoRA tokens, and near-zero cost for batches with no LoRA tokens.

#48421 has since merged the minimal fix for the `-1` aliasing bug this PR originally targeted, so, as suggested on #48421, I've rebased onto it and kept the title for continuity. The correctness fix and its regression test now come from #48421; this PR changes only how the work is done. The description above predates this; the current scope is:

**1. Skip no-LoRA rows instead of computing and masking them** (`vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py`)

#48421 clamps the index to 0, runs the gather + einsum for every row, then zeroes the `-1` rows. The gather materializes a per-token copy of the LoRA weights, so base-model tokens pay the full LoRA cost. The CPU decode path also has no `no_lora` early return (prefill does), so a decode batch with no LoRA tokens still runs shrink/expand in every LoRA layer.

This PR selects only valid rows before the gather + einsum in `bgmv_shrink` / `bgmv_expand` / `bgmv_expand_slice`, and returns immediately when no row has an active adapter. Semantics match #48421 and the Triton kernels: no-LoRA rows are left untouched (including under `add_inputs=False`). When every row is valid, the original code path runs unchanged.

**2. Group `add_shrink` by LoRA** (`vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py`)

Replaces the per-slice loop (`# TODO fuse these kernels`) for multi-slice layers (e.g. packed qkv) with one GEMM per active LoRA against its concatenated A slices, with tokens sorted by LoRA. This avoids per-token weight copies entirely for shrink, which dominate cost as the batch grows. Single-slice layers keep the existing path.

**3. Benchmark** — `benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py` times `PunicaWrapperCPU.add_lora_linear` (shrink + expand) in the decode path across batch sizes and LoRA/base-model token mixes.

`torch.compile` note: the CPU platform sets `CompilationMode.NONE` whenever LoRA is enabled (`vllm/platforms/cpu.py`), so the data-dependent shapes here don't introduce graph breaks.

### Not a duplicate

#48421 (merged) fixed the correctness bug with clamp + mask; this PR keeps its semantics and its regression test (`test_torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens`) and changes only how the work is done. My original aliasing tests were dropped as redundant with that test. No other open PR touches `PunicaWrapperCPU` or the torch bgmv ops. #47951 (open) skips the whole LoRA layer path in eager mode when a batch has no active adapter, but only wires that up for the GPU/XPU wrappers; it would be complementary here (layer-level skip for all-base-model batches) and doesn't cover mixed batches or the shrink grouping.

### Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/lora/test_punica_ops.py -k torch_ops_bgmv_skips_no_lora_tokens
pre-commit run --files vllm/lora/ops/torch_ops/lora_ops.py \
    vllm/lora/punica_wrapper/punica_cpu.py benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py
python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py --max-loras 1 --iters 200
python benchmarks/kernels/cpu/benchmark_cpu_lora.py --max-loras 4 --iters 200
```

Plus an out-of-tree equivalence check against #48421's implementation:
- bgmv ops: all-valid / mixed / all-`-1` batches, fp32 + bf16, `add_inputs` True/False — outputs identical (`torch.equal`).
- grouped `add_shrink` vs. the per-slice loop: decode and prefill metadata, 2–3 slices, bf16 inputs into fp32 buffers, buffers pre-filled with random values to confirm `-1` rows are untouched — `assert_close` passes; empty batch handled.

`tests/lora/test_layers.py` exercises `add_shrink` end to end on CPU (`test_column_parallel_packed`, `test_merged_column_parallel_variable_slice`), but it couldn't run in my local environment (fails identically on unmodified main); relying on CI for those.
